Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables. Find $\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=1]$ given that the conditional probability mass function ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,1)$ is shown in the table above and the corresponding conditional expected value is ${\mu }_{Y|1}=3.3.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=x] & =\text{E}[(Y-{\mu }_{Y|x})^{2}\,|\,X=x] \\  & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=x]-{\mu }_{Y|x}^{2} \\  & =[{\sum }_{y}{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)]-{\mu }_{Y|x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=1] & =[{\sum }_{y}{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,1)]-{\mu }_{Y|1}^{2} \\  & =[(2)^{2}\cdot 0.35+(4)^{2}\cdot 0.65]-{(3.3)}^{2} \\  & =1.4+10.4-10.89 \\  & =0.91.\end{aligned}
$$

| $X=2$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ |

Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables. Find $\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=2]$ given that $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above and the corresponding conditional expected value is ${\mu }_{Y|2}=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=x] & =\text{E}[(Y-{\mu }_{Y|x})^{2}\,|\,X=x] \\  & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=x]-{\mu }_{Y|x}^{2} \\  & =[{\sum }_{y}{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)]-{\mu }_{Y|x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In order to find ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x),$ let's first find the marginal distribution for $X,$ corresponding to the row totals: 

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ | ${f}_{X}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{3}{16}$ | $\frac{1}{16}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |
| $X=2$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |

The conditional probability mass function of $Y$ given that $X=x$ is

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)}.
$$

Therefore, dividing each joint probability by the corresponding row total, we obtain the conditional probability mass function of $Y$ given that $X=x:$

| ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $1$ |
| $X=2$ | $\frac{3}{4}$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $1$ |

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=2] & =[{\sum }_{y}{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,2)]-{\mu }_{Y|2}^{2} \\  & =[{0}^{2}\cdot \frac{3}{4}+{2}^{2}\cdot 0+{4}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{4}]-{1}^{2} \\  & =0+0+4-1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $Y$ given $X=x$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y\,|\,X=x] & =\text{E}[(Y-{\mu }_{Y|x})^{2}\,|\,X=x] \\  & =\text{E}[{Y}^{2}\,|\,X=x]-{\mu }_{Y|x}^{2} \\  & =[{\sum }_{y}{y}^{2}\,{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)]-{\mu }_{Y|x}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In order to find ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x),$ let's first find the marginal distribution for $X,$ corresponding to the row totals: 

| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ | ${f}_{X}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{5}{8}$ |
| $X=2$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ |

The conditional probability mass function of $Y$ given that $X=x$ is

$$
{f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{X}(x)}.

Therefore, dividing each joint probability by the corresponding row total, we obtain the conditional probability mass function of $Y$ given that $X=x:$

| ${f}_{Y|X}(y\,|\,x)$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $\frac{4}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $1$ |
| $X=2$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{2}{3}$ | $1$ |

$$

Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables. Find $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=4]$ given that the random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above and the corresponding conditional expected value is ${\mu }_{X|4}=\frac{3}{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2} \\  & =[{\sum }_{x}{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In order to find ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y),$ let's first find the marginal distribution of $Y,$ corresponding to the column totals: 

| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ |
| $X=2$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{12}$ |
| $X=3$ | $\frac{1}{12}$ | $\frac{1}{12}$ |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ |

The conditional probability mass function of $X$ given that $Y=y$ is

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=\frac{f(x,y)}{{f}_{Y}(y)}.
$$

Therefore, dividing each joint probability by the corresponding column total, we obtain the conditional probability mass function of $X$ given that $Y=y:$

| ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $\frac{1}{3}$ | $\frac{2}{3}$ |
| $X=2$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ |
| $X=3$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ |
|  | $1$ | $1$ |

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=4] & =[{\sum }_{x}{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,4)]-{\mu }_{X|4}^{2} \\  & =[{1}^{2}\cdot \frac{2}{3}+{2}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{6}+{3}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{6}]-{(\frac{3}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{3}{2}-\frac{9}{4} \\  & =\frac{7}{12}.\end{aligned}
$$
